title: Cost allocation smoothing for interleaved multi-route requests
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Background: Our current per-request token mapper attributes every generated token to the immediate active route/model, which leads to noisy cost spikes when a single client session interleaves multiple routes (e.g., chat + embedding + rerank) or when KV-cache hits change effective compute per token. This ticket implements a smoothing layer in the usage pipeline that produces more representative per-route cost shares while preserving auditability and determinism for billing reconciliation.
goals: Introduce a windowed attribution step that amortizes cost across closely-timed interleaved requests from the same session/tenant
Make the smoothing deterministic and explainable for downstream invoices and refunds
Fail-safe: preserve exact per-request raw tokens in cold path for audits and disputes
Ship observability surfaced in Console: delta vs raw, smoothing ratio, affected customers
non_goals: Change pricing tiers or discounts as part of this work
Replace the ledger system — this is upstream of ledger ingestion
technical_approach: Add a streaming enrichment stage (Beam or Flink) before the cost-join that groups events by session_id with a short time-window (configurable, default 10s). Compute per-event compute estimate (model variant, seq_len, cache_hit boolean) and produce a smoothed allocation vector across routes in the window using a weighted amortization formula: weight = effective_compute^(alpha) where alpha is tunable. Emit both raw_token_records (unchanged) and smoothed_allocation_records (route, tokens_allocated, compute_estimate, window_id, deterministic_hash). Downstream ledger joins prefer smoothed_allocation_records; an admin flag enables bypass to raw records for dispute workflows.
schema_changes: Add 'allocation_fraction' (float as string) to document how tokens were split
consistency_and_audit: To remain auditable we keep a 1:1 mapping between raw events and produced allocation rows. Each allocation row includes pointers back to raw event ids and the deterministic_hash used to compute allocations so the same input always yields the same output. A compact provenance view will be added to Console that shows raw -> allocation diffs for any invoice line item.
implementation_plan: Prototype smoothing operator in a Beam job using historical traffic sample (sprint 1)
Implement config flags and alpha tuning via Feature Flags service (sprint 1)
Add deterministic hashing and explicit window_id generation (sprint 2)
Deploy to staging streaming pipeline, run side-by-side with current pipeline for 48h to collect diffs (sprint 2)
Gradual rollout via data-plane routing: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% by tenant groups (sprint 3)
Add Console dashboard tiles and alerting for smoothing_ratio, revenue_delta, and audit_requests (sprint 3)
Full cutover and update billing-run job to accept smoothed allocations (release window)
Post-launch: run two-week shadow billing for top 50 customers and validate refunds if necessary
acceptance_criteria: Beam job emits allocation rows with window_id and deterministic_hash for 99.9% of input events
No more than 0.5% of allocations are dropped or malformed in staging shadow run
Smoothing produces reduced per-route variance for interleaved sessions by at least 30% on sampled workload
Audit trail UI surfaces raw vs smoothed allocation for any chosen invoice line
Rollback path exists that forces downstream ledger ingestion to raw allocation rows
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-smoothing could obscure real heavy usage. Mitigation: alpha tuning + conservative defaults + per-tenant opt-out
Risk: Increased pipeline latency. Mitigation: make operator cheap (bounded window), run in parallel and measure p99; provide circuit-breaker to bypass smoothing if latencySLO breached
Risk: Determinism mismatch across job restarts. Mitigation: use explicit window_id and deterministic hashing seeded from tenant_id + ingestion_timestamp
migration_and_rollout: Stage 0: local prototype using replayed event dumps
Stage 1: staging streaming job side-by-side shadowing (no ledger effect)
Stage 2: 1% tenants using smoothed allocations for reporting only
Stage 3: expand rollout with automated checks and rollback on unacceptable revenue deltas
Stage 4: full production and start 2-week shadow billing for top customers
docs_and_communication: Customer-facing KB: 'Why your billing looks different after allocation smoothing' (draft)
Release notes entry for console-2026.03 describing opt-out and audit UI
